text:
alex: Heads-up — our H100 canary pool in us-west2 started throwing PTX/JIT warnings and a handful of OOMs right after the driver rollout (today morning).
maria: saw that — which driver did the rollout push? :eyes:
alex: deploy-bot shows node image bumped to nvidia-driver 546.38 and CUDA 12.4. Canary label is h100-canary-1.
kai: logs look like PTX mismatch/jit fallback noise, then a couple of kernels failing to launch. snippet:
```
[2026-03-17 09:12:42] cudaGetLastError(): unspecified launch failure
ptxas warning : function _attention_kernel compiled for sm_90, kernel requires sm_90
PTX JIT: falling back to interpreter
```
jen: also getting NCCL WARNs on some ranks during all-reduce in canary jobs.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-112 (h100 canary jit/ptx regressions).
alex: early impact: 3/40 canary GPUs had >10% latency p95 regressions, a couple of single-run OOMs. Not cluster-wide yet.
maria: this smells like a kernel->driver compatibility issue. Our runtime expects SM90 kernels with specific PTX capability. Did we also roll a new compiler or CUDA toolkit inside the image?
kai: image change included nvcc 12.4 but we didn't change model containers. Most images still have model runtime compiled against cuda 12.3 ABI.
jen: could be the JIT now refusing to accept older ptx or generating different codepaths. We saw similar once with a Hopper microcode mismatch.
sre-oncall: recommend pause canary rollout to other regions, pin scheduling to existing nodes, and throttle new H100 provisioning.
alex: agreed — I'm pausing the automated canary schedule and disabling new nodes in us-west2 via autoscaler policy.
maria: can we quickly confirm driver minimums? I remember a note: driver >= 545.x for SM90 features. If we require >=546.38 maybe some kernel path changed.
kai: checking vendor notes now. NV release says: recommended driver 546+ for full SM90 PTX support; but some older PTX (compiled against 12.3) might JIT differently.
jen: quick mitigation: force model containers to use precompiled kernels (AOT) where possible, or pin to the previous driver and revert nodes.
alex: rollback plan: cordon nodes with 546.38, spin up older image (545.20) pool, migrate canary workloads. Ops-team: how long to reprovision ~10 H100s in us-west2 with old image?
ops-bot: reprovision estimate: 18-30 minutes per node; parallel up to 8 nodes concurrently due to quota.
sre-oncall: if reprovision is slow, we should fallback to model-level workarounds: reduce batch sizes to avoid OOMs and set env CUDA_DISABLE_PTX_JIT=1 for non-JIT workloads (where safe).
maria: note: CUDA_DISABLE_PTX_JIT=1 will fail if kernels only exist as PTX — need to verify per image.
alex: I'm collecting sample traces and will upload to the infra bucket: gs://redwood-infra/h100-canary/1834567890/traces.tar.gz
kai: also seeing NCCL timeout 3000ms on multi-GPU tests after the drift — maybe driver change altered interconnect behavior.
jen: if NCCL regressions persist, we may need to revert both driver and NCCL or adjust GDR settings on the hosts.
sre-oncall: action items:
- alex: collect traces + node lists (in progress)
- kai: vendor ticket to NVIDIA with logs and PTX samples
- maria: coordinate rollback image for us-west2 and estimate capacity impact
- ops: block further driver rollouts to other regions
- jen: prepare container workarounds and quick config toggles
alex: tagging priority P1 for canary; will update thread when I have node list and repro steps.
ops-bot: Rotation note: @sre-oncall has been paged for follow-up.
maria: also note cost impact: if we reprovision and run double pools we will see short-term capacity costs. flag finance if >48h.
kai: vendor response pending, but starting initial bisect: kernel ABI vs ptx vs driver microcode.
alex: thanks — if anyone sees new OOMs or increases in p95 please paste sample logs here. Otherwise I'll post the rollback timeline shortly. :thumbsup:
